text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Workload 96x192x96 FP16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation; shared-memory estimate max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages,4*block_M*block_N), capped at 32768 for portability and below the 49152 hard max. Domains kept broad (block_M {32,64,128}, block_N {64,128}, block_K {32,64}, stages {1,2,3}, threads 128, swizzle {0,4,8,16}); the divide constraint prunes tuples whose tiles do not divide M=96,N=192,K=96, so feasible points include block_M=32 or 64 (96/64 not integer, so 64 is filtered), block_N=64 (128 does not divide 192, filtered), block_K=32 (64 does not divide 96, filtered). Prior attempts 00 and 01 both selected block_M=32,block_N=64,block_K=32,stages=1 with swizzle 0 then 16, each yielding identical simulated 3.6996us (8 blocks/SM, 0 DRAM MB, 8192 smem bytes, 58 regs) — swizzle had no observable effect, consistent with min(swizzle,ceil(M/block_M)) saturating at ceil(96/32)=3 so swizzle 4/8/16 all give reuse=3 versus swizzle 0 giving reuse=1, yet no simulator latency change; this suggests the analytic traffic hypothesis is not materializing for this small workload and simulated DRAM is already zero, so traffic weight is less relevant. I keep swizzle {0,4,8,16} allowed to test with other tile/stage combos, keep equal weights since no dimension has yet shown dominance, and hold the 32768 cap. Next hypothesis: vary block_K and num_stages (e.g., num_stages=2/3 or block_K=64) may shift pipeline/footprint costs and alter simulated latency more than swizzle did; if further swizzle changes remain flat in simulator I will down-weight traffic and up-weight pipeline/footprint. No global optimality claimed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal numeric checks execute exact source/config/TIR but do not execute the CUDA binary."}
